title: Angular Architecture 🏛️
description: Understand the big picture: modules, components, templates, services, and DI.

slides.title: The Big Picture 🖼️
slides.content:
# Angular Application Anatomy

Every Angular app is built from the same fundamental building blocks:

1. **Modules** – containers for a set of related capabilities.
2. **Components** – control a patch of the screen (view + logic).
3. **Templates** – the HTML that defines the component’s UI.
4. **Services** – reusable logic (data fetching, logging).
5. **Dependency Injection (DI)** – supplies services to components.

quizData.question: Which Angular building block defines a view (a piece of the screen)?
quizData.explanation: Components control a view – a portion of the screen – through their template.

slides.title: Modules: The Organisers 📦
slides.content:
An Angular module (NgModule) groups components, directives, pipes, and services that belong together.

* The **root module** (`AppModule`) bootstraps the app.
* You can create **feature modules** (e.g., `UserModule`) for better organisation.
* Use the `@NgModule` decorator to declare what belongs to the module.

slides.title: Root Module Example
Components: The View & Logic 🧩
slides.content:
A component = TypeScript class + template + styles.

* The class holds data (properties) and behaviour (methods).
* The template (HTML) defines the UI, using data binding to connect to the class.
* Styles can be scoped to the component.

Every Angular app has at least one component – the root component.

quizData.question: A component in Angular always needs a separate CSS file.
quizData.explanation: A component can have inline styles using `styles` array or link to an external stylesheet, but it’s not mandatory to have a separate file.

slides.title: Services & DI: The Worker Bees 🐝
slides.content:
Services are classes with a focused purpose (e.g., fetching data).

* They are typically **singletons** – one instance shared across the app.
* **Dependency Injection (DI)** automatically provides a service to a component that asks for it (by listing it in the constructor).
* This keeps your components lean and focused on the view.

slides.title: Analogy: Restaurant 🍽️
slides.content:
Think of your Angular app as a restaurant:

* **Module** = the menu sections (starters, mains).
* **Component** = a waiter (handles a table and its order).
* **Template** = the plate presentation.
* **Service** = the kitchen (prepares food).
* **DI** = the food runner (delivers dishes where needed).
